content: In a browser-driving script, assert on element counts before reading them. A step that silently does nothing — a sign-in guarded by `if (await page.getByPlaceholder(/email/i).count())` when the fields carry labels instead — leaves every later query returning 0, `[]`, or "not found", which reads as a clean run rather than a failure. Make the script exit non-zero when a precondition it depends on is absent (`if (url.includes("/sign-in")) process.exit(1)`).
context: Verifying ISS-007/ISS-008/ISS-010 in the 3afya web app. The first Playwright run reported "PICKER INPUT: 0", "GROUPING BUTTONS: 0", "CHIPS: []" and no console errors — which looked like the features were missing. They were not: the sign-in block had been skipped because the inputs are labelled rather than placeholdered, so every assertion ran against the sign-in page. Adding an explicit post-login URL check turned the same script into a real verification, and all four screens then passed.
title: A UI check that cannot fail is not a check — assert the page is what you think it is
